claims.source_value: Governor's Bay (lower river, below Ottawa) 1971, back-calculated TL at annuli 1–4: females 126, 160, 195, 222 mm; males 127, 162, 196, 222. The upper river (Shirleys and Britannia bays, Lac Deschênes) grew much faster: males 142, 199, 253, 284; females 131, 177, 223, 271 (Table 17)
claims.location: p. 99 (PDF p. 130), Table 19; p. 97 (PDF p. 128), Table 17
claims.conditions: pectoral-spine back-calculation (Lee–Lea formula, 13-mm intercept); Governor's Bay sample mostly ages III–VI (males: II 1, III 16, IV 36, V 46, VI 13, VII 2); 'total length at the end of each year of life'
claims.note: the paper's 161 at age 2 mixes the sexes (160 F, 162 M); name the station, or give the sexes separately. More important: this is the slow lower-river station (see the next claim)

claims.claim: brown bullheads pass 20 cm only at about the third annulus even in a fast-growing Ottawa River population
claims.source_value: the third-annulus figure (195–196 mm) is from Governor's Bay in the lower river, where growth was 'much less' than upstream and which Rubec read as overpopulated; in the fast-growing upper river males reached 199 mm at the 2nd annulus and females 223 mm at the 3rd (177 at the 2nd)
claims.location: p. 94 (PDF p. 123); p. 120 (PDF p. 153); Tables 17 and 19 (PDF pp. 128, 130); study area p. 4 (PDF p. 18)
claims.quote: The lower river data would tend to indicate that the species has overpopulated
claims.conditions: Governor's Bay is one of the lower-river bays (Brewery Creek, Hay Bay, Governor's Bay, Kettle Is. Bay) below the Chaudière Falls; p. 94: growth greatest in the upper river at Shirleys and Britannia bays, lower-river growth 'much less'
claims.note: 'even in a fast-growing population' is backwards for the numbers used. With upper-river growth (20 cm at about the 2nd annulus) the share of a stock surviving ~50 %/yr that is under 20 cm would be nearer 50–75 % than 70–80 % (project arithmetic to be redone in the rewrite); Rubec's first annulus (~127 mm at Governor's Bay) also looks large for age 1, as the project notes say

claims.claim: most published bullhead studies concern 'overcrowded and stunted populations' (Rubec 1975, citing Carlander 1969)
claims.location: p. 120 (PDF p. 153), Age and Growth, Discussion
claims.quote: Most studies of bullhead have been on overcrowded and stunted populations (Carlander, 1969)
claims.note: Rubec continues that the upper-river and Hawkesbury fish had not exceeded carrying capacity while 'the lower river data would tend to indicate that the species has overpopulated that section of river'

notes: The growth numbers the paper uses are the slow lower-river station (Governor's Bay), not a fast-growing population; the upper-river fish (Table 17) passed 20 cm about a year earlier. Other useful values (abstract, p. x): densities of 2,500–7,800 bullhead/ha in Kettle Island Bay; bullhead 41.6 % of all fish above Ottawa and 85.9 % below; tagged fish mostly stayed in a home bay; dominance fights wound 5–17 % of fish in the spawning season; muscle mercury generally < 0.5 ppm. p. 72: most bullhead over age three were sexually mature; only 17 pairs spawned successfully at Brewery Creek in 1971, and ~30 % of mature females at Governor's Bay were resorbing eggs. p. 119: Ottawa River growth usually better than US and Czechoslovak populations; density and food mattered more than latitude. Length–weight (lower river, 1973, p. 119): Hay Bay 'log W = −5.210 + 3.121 TL' as printed (presumably log TL), r = 0.963, n = 100. Condition factors by month and section in Table 35 (p. 117).
